beats.narration: If your backend code calls Stripe directly inside your order service, swapping payment providers means rewriting core checkout logic. Abstraction separates what an operation promises to do from how it works behind the scenes.

beats.title: Abstract Classes: Partial Blueprints

steps.explanation: Cannot be instantiated directly with new; represents an incomplete shared base concept.
Concrete method inherited and shared by all concrete subclasses.
No method body; forces every concrete subclass to supply its own implementation.

beats.narration: An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly with new. It holds shared state and concrete helper methods, while leaving abstract methods bodyless so every concrete subclass supplies its own specific export logic.

beats.title: Concrete Subclasses vs. Direct Instantiation

top.label: Direct Instantiation
top.code:
// Fails at compile time!
ReportGenerator gen = new ReportGenerator("Q4");

bottom.label: CsvReportGenerator
points: Invokes super(...) to initialize base fields
Supplies body for all abstract methods

beats.narration: Attempting to instantiate an abstract class directly triggers a compile error. Subclasses like CsvReportGenerator call super to initialize base fields and implement all missing abstract methods.

beats.title: Part 1 Locked In
takeaways: Abstraction decouples contracts from implementation details
Abstract classes combine shared state with abstract hooks
Concrete subclasses must implement all abstract methods

parts.partTitle: Template Workflows & The Constructor Overridable Trap

beats.headline: Why super constructors trigger NullPointerExceptions.
beats.subline: Calling an abstract method inside a base constructor crashes before subclass fields exist.
beats.narration: Calling an overridable method inside an abstract class constructor looks harmless. But runtime polymorphic dispatch will invoke subclass logic before subclass fields are initialized, throwing a silent NullPointerException.

beats.title: Template Method: Enforcing Guardrails

steps.explanation: Marked final so subclasses cannot override, reorder, or skip auth and audit checks.
Subclasses customize only the specific ledger posting logic.

beats.narration: The Template Method pattern marks the workflow method final so subclasses cannot skip auth or audit steps. Subclasses provide code only for the protected abstract hook method.

beats.title: The Constructor Overridable Method Trap

top.label: Overridable Constructor Call
points: dest is still null when initialize() runs

bottom.label: Safe Helper Initialization
points: Only call private or final methods in constructors

beats.narration: When AuditService calls super, BaseService constructor triggers initialize. But AuditService fields are still null. Never call non-final overridable methods inside constructors.

beats.title: Subclass Initialization Dispatch Trace
beats.caption: Exact order of JVM constructor execution

lines.text: # 1. Allocate AuditService memory (all fields set to null)
Exception: java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot read field dest
Rule: Subclass field initializers run AFTER super() returns!

beats.narration: Here is the exact trace. Memory is allocated with default null fields, super runs first, dynamically dispatches to the subclass method, and crashes because the field initializer hasn't executed yet.

beats.title: Part 2 Mastered
takeaways: Use final template methods to freeze execution order
Never call overridable methods inside constructors
Subclass fields remain null while super() executes

parts.partTitle: Multiple Inheritance of Types & Modern Interface Features

beats.headline: Java forbids multi-class inheritance—here is why.
beats.subline: State diamond conflicts destroy memory layouts, but interface type composition is completely safe.
beats.narration: If a class could extend multiple classes with state, inherited field conflicts would wreck memory layouts. Interfaces solve this by offering multiple inheritance of types without carrying instance state.

beats.title: Evolution of Java Interfaces
beats.subtitle: From pure contracts to modern sealed abstractions

beats.narration: Interfaces evolved dramatically. Java 8 added default and static methods for API evolution. Java 9 introduced private helpers to deduplicate code, and Java 17 brought sealed types for closed domain modeling.

beats.title: Multiple Inheritance of Types

steps.explanation: Exportable extends both Auditable and Retryable interfaces seamlessly.
InvoiceJob satisfies multiple interface contracts without state collision.

beats.narration: A class can implement multiple interfaces, and interfaces can extend multiple parent interfaces. Because interfaces do not hold per-instance fields, Java guarantees clean type polymorphism without state collisions.

beats.title: Private Interface Methods (Java 9+)

steps.explanation: Public default methods share common underlying formatting logic.
Java 9+ internal helpers hidden from callers and implementing classes.

beats.narration: Java 9 allowed private and private static methods inside interfaces. Now default methods can share formatting and sanitization logic internally without polluting the public contract.

takeaways: Interfaces enable multiple type inheritance without state collisions
Default methods let you extend existing APIs safely
Private interface methods encapsulate internal helper logic

parts.partTitle: Default Method Conflicts, Sealed Interfaces & Cheat Sheet

beats.headline: What happens when two interfaces share a default method?
beats.subline: javac halts with a compile error unless you know the 3 conflict resolution rules.
beats.narration: If two implemented interfaces define identical default methods, javac halts with a compile error. You must know Java's three resolution rules to fix the diamond collision cleanly.

beats.title: Resolving Default Method Diamond Conflicts

top.label: Ambiguous Default Collision
points: javac cannot guess which default method to invoke
Unrelated default methods clash at compile time

bottom.label: Explicit Resolution Syntax
points: Class implementation always overrides interface defaults

beats.narration: When two unrelated interfaces declare identical default methods, compilation fails. Resolve it by overriding the method and using InterfaceName dot super dot methodName to explicitly select the behavior you want.

beats.title: Sealed Interfaces (Java 17+)

steps.explanation: Restricts implementation exclusively to permitted records or classes.
Enables Java 21+ switch pattern matching to verify all cases without default clauses.

beats.narration: Sealed interfaces restrict which classes can implement them using permits. This creates closed domain hierarchies, enabling Java 21 switch expressions to check exhaustiveness without requiring dummy default clauses.

beats.title: Abstract Class vs Interface Decision Matrix

top.label: Abstract Class
top.code:
// Use when components share state or Skeletal logic:
- Requires instance fields (mutable / final)
- Single inheritance (extends base class)
- Protected / package-private template methods
points: Best for closely related classes sharing instance fields

bottom.label: Interface
bottom.code:
// Use for public service contracts & capabilities:
- Pure contracts without instance state
- Multiple inheritance of types (implements)
- Default, static & private helper methods
points: Default choice for public APIs and service contracts
Enables loose coupling and easy mocking in tests

beats.narration: Reach for abstract classes when you need shared instance state, non-public methods, or template workflows. Choose interfaces for pure capabilities, public service contracts, and decoupled multi-type APIs.
